slides.say: A review answers one question for the reader: should I try it, or not?

slides.foot: for readers like you — lively, personal, honest
slides.say: In Part 2 you might review a film, a book, a restaurant, an app or a place. You write for the readers of a magazine or website, people like you. So be lively, personal and honest.

lines: Recommend it — or warn people off
slides.say: Every review does three things. Introduce it. Describe what stands out. And recommend it, or warn people off.
One hundred and forty to one hundred and ninety words. Four paragraphs.

slides.head: A · Catch the reader
slides.frame: Choosing a … can be a real challenge. However, … is certainly an option worth considering.
slides.ex: Choosing a restaurant can be a real challenge. However, Café Azul is certainly an option worth considering.
slides.say: Your first paragraph has two jobs. First, catch the reader. Pick a line from column A. Choosing a restaurant can be a real challenge. However, Café Azul is certainly an option worth considering.

slides.head: B · Introduce it
slides.frame: Known / famous for its …, … has been a favourite among …
slides.ex: Known for its homemade cakes, it has been a favourite among teenagers for years.
slides.say: Second, introduce it. Say what it is and why people know it. Known for its homemade cakes, it has been a favourite among teenagers for years.

slides.big: Name it in the first two lines.
slides.sub: — and keep writing about IT, all the way to the end.
slides.say: Name the thing in the first two lines, and keep writing about it all the way to the end. A reader who doesn't know what you're reviewing stops reading.
Now the body. Two paragraphs, one feature each.

slides.head: 1 · Name it   2 · Describe it
slides.frame: What impressed me most was … which is absolutely …
slides.ex: What impressed me most was the food, which is absolutely mouth-watering.
slides.say: Step one, name the feature. Step two, describe it. What impressed me most was the food, which is absolutely mouth-watering. This is where your adjectives live.

slides.head: Then one or two of these
lines: This is because everything is made fresh.
For instance, the banana cake is still warm.
The only drawback is that it gets crowded.
slides.say: Then choose one or two of these. A reason: this is because everything is made fresh. An example: for instance, the banana cake is still warm. Or a contrast: the only drawback is that it gets crowded.
A fair review gives one negative too. It makes your praise believable. Tap Paragraph structure to see all six steps.
The last paragraph answers the reader's question. Should I go?

slides.head: Recommend it
slides.frame: For anyone who is interested in …, … is a must.
slides.ex: For anyone who is interested in good coffee, Café Azul is a must.
slides.say: Pick a line from Recommendation. For anyone who is interested in good coffee, Café Azul is a must. Say who will love it, and why, in one short sentence.
Never add a new feature here. And never end with: that's all, thank you for reading.

slides.sub: test yourself on a real review question
slides.say: Now open the Workout, and test yourself on a real review question.
